improvementsForChallenger: The ground is a single flat olive-mustard fill with faint noise; there is no grass, no texture, no light falloff that reads as terrain. Replace it with an actual meadow surface (grass tufts, flowers, mowed-path value variation) — right now it reads as a UI background color, not a place.

Nothing casts a shadow: cards, the fence, and every perimeter rock/tree float on the ground plane. Add grounded contact shadows with one consistent sun direction; the fence in the top-left corner especially looks pasted on.

The perimeter 'environment' is unresolved: the corner crops (bl, br, tr) are abstract near-black and mud-brown polyhedra with no material identity — I could not tell rocks from bushes from trees. Give them albedo/lighting so they read as foliage and stone, and vary silhouettes.

Cards have zero edge thickness — they are flat rectangles. The hand cards also show a teal under-border sticking out on one side like a misregistered layer; either make that an intentional sleeve with even margins or remove it.

The stream in field-corner-tl/br is a hard-edged cyan ribbon with three flat bands and aliased edges; it looks like a masking-tape strip. It needs banks, softened edges, and lighting consistent with the scene.

The center divider is a clean glow line, but it sits on featureless ground so it reads as an HTML hr with bloom. Once the terrain is real, let the seam interact with it (scorched/blessed grass, irregular falloff) instead of a perfectly uniform gradient.
The ground is a flat, untextured olive-mustard gradient that reads as a UI background, not a meadow — add grass texture, tonal variation, flowers, and worn paths so the playfield reads as terrain.

Environment props (rocks, trees, stream) are unshaded near-black low-poly silhouettes with zero cast shadows; the corner crops show raw facets floating on a void. Establish one sun direction and give every prop a grounded shadow and lit/shadow faces.

Cards have no physical presence: no edge thickness, only a faint uniform halo instead of a contact shadow (see field-card-contact — Duskfang floats). Add card-stock extrusion and a directional grounded shadow consistent with the scene light.
The palette is muddy — mustard field against near-black props with no atmosphere or warm sunlight grading; introduce a coherent golden-hour grade tying cards, ground, and props together.
The stream is two flat cyan ribbon bands with no highlights, banks, or interaction with the surrounding rocks; it reads as a decal, not water.
The divider is a clean glow line but sits on dead-flat ground, which makes the whole center of the field feel like empty negative space; give the seam something to interact with.
